node-1.label: Patient has recurrent ankle swelling, painful nodules on legs and feet, progression to painful leg ulcers, and oral and vaginal ulcerations

node-2.label: A 30-year-old woman has a 15-year history of recurrent ankle swelling and intermittent painful and tender nodules on legs and feet; symptoms worsened during two pregnancies carried to term.

node-3.label: One and a half years before admission, nodules progressed to painful leg ulcers and she developed intermittent oral and vaginal ulcerations; previous treatments included wound care, leg compression, systemic corticosteroids, methotrexate, hydroxychloroquine, aspirin, and rivaroxaban.

node-4.label: Physical examination showed large, extremely tender, irregularly shaped circumferential leg ulcers with violaceous and purpuric borders, areas of eschar, and fibrinous base; reticulated erythema and purpura on hands; faintly erythematous blanching macules and papules coalescing into patches and thin plaques on bilateral thighs; genital and oral ulcers present.
